label: verify-bm-formlabs-printing-workflows

claims.claim: Form 4 uses a single resin tank and cartridge per print; changing resin type means changing both, so a two-resin strip needs two prints.
claims.source_says: Changing resin types between prints: When changing resin types, always change both the resin tank and resin cartridge.
claims.note: Quote is in the Form 4 manual; 'two prints' is a reasonable inference from it.

claims.claim: Open Material Mode is a paid per-printer licence needed for any non-Formlabs resin; stock Formlabs resins do not need it.
claims.source_says: With Open Material Mode, you can print with any type of 405 nm photopolymer resin on Formlabs SLA printers. Open Material Mode is available for a one-time lifetime fee per printer.
claims.note: The per-printer fee and non-Formlabs-resin use are stated; 'needed' and 'stock resins do not need it' are implied, not said.

claims.claim: Elastic/Flexible 50A takes up 39.2% mass in IPA in 24 h (1 cm cube) vs <0.1% for Rigid 10K; solvent is a far stronger stimulus than humidity.
claims.source_says: Elastic 50A Resin V2 ... IPA 39.2 (10th column); Rigid 10K Resin IPA <0.1; weight gain % after 24 hours, 1 cm cubes. Water for Elastic 50A V2: 0.7.
claims.note: Numbers reproduce from the table; the humidity comparison rests on the water column (0.7), which is liquid water, not humidity.

claims.claim: A strip printed flat on the build platform loses about 0.1 mm of thickness to first-layer compression, half of a 0.2 mm layer, so thickness must be measured.
claims.source_says: When printing a model directly on the build platform, expect each model to be approximately 0.1 mm shorter than designed along the Z-axis in the model's first layers. The exact compressed height varies between printers.
claims.note: 0.1 mm is stated; the half-layer comparison is simple arithmetic and the measure-it advice is a judgment.

overall: All four claims hold against the live Formlabs pages and manual. One is partly supported: the Open Material Mode page gives the fee and the any-405-nm-resin scope, but not the 'needed' framing.
